title: Decision Breadcrumbs: Chained Routing Context and Per-Hop Metrics for Fallback Explainability
creator: Aisha Martinez
description:
Summary: Add a compact, human- and machine-readable 'decision breadcrumb' record that captures chained routing context for each inference request. Breadcrumbs should include per-hop timing, policy scores, region/tier decisions, model-variant mappings, and fallback triggers so engineers can reconstruct exactly why a request was routed the way it was and what fallback sequence executed. This ticket scopes the telemetry schema, sampling/retention policy, console integration, and a lightweight ingest path for high-throughput hosted traffic.

Why: Current traces and per-hop metrics exist but are fragmented across services and lack a single artifact that represents the routing chain with normalized fields (scores, reasons, tenant constraints, candidate variants). That makes debugging fallback behavior and root-causing SLO regressions slow, especially when requests cross regions or downgrade model variants for cost/latency. Breadcrumbs will improve incident MTTR, make regression alerts actionable, and enable post-hoc quality analysis for fallback sequences.

Non-goals: This ticket does not implement full request-level payload capture, long-term cold storage of every breadcrumb, or heavy-weight causal analysis pipelines. Those can be follow-ups once core schema and console UI are validated.
acceptance_criteria: Every routed request includes a decision_breadcrumb ID in existing request traces in staging (sampled) and production (sampling rate configurable).

Breadcrumb record contains canonical fields: decision_id, timestamp, route_hops (ordered list as compact string), per_hop_latency_ms, selected_model_variant, selection_policy, policy_scores (normalized), fallback_reason, region, tier, capacity_tier, and trace_link.
Console shows a per-request breadcrumb panel that visualizes the hop chain and highlights fallback hop with reason and latency.
Alerting rule exists to surface increased fallback frequency or long breadcrumb chain durations across a rolling 5m window for a customer with high SLO risk.
Storage respects PII and tenant isolation: breadcrumbs do not include prompt/response content unless redaction/opt-in is enabled via tenant config.
Sampling and retention controls are configurable with defaults that limit cost for free-tier customers.
implementation_notes:
High-level approach: 1) Define compact breadcrumb schema (string-safe, CSV-friendly for event streams). 2) Inject breadcrumb span/field from routing service at decision points; each hop appends a compact token describing node_id|policy|score|chosen_variant|latency_ms; hops concatenated in order. 3) Emit a final breadcrumb event to telemetry pipeline with decision_id and summary fields; include link to full trace/span ids. 4) Add sampling knobs in routing config (percent, deterministic by tenant hash) and retention tiering upstream. 5) Console: lightweight renderer that expands tokens into human labels and maps chosen_variant IDs to model names via catalog lookup.

Schema (textual representation): decision_id (uuid string), root_ts (ISO8601), hops_token (pipe-separated hop tokens), hops_token example = "node42|region-us-east1|policy-latency|score=0.92|variant=redwood-7b-q|lat=8", fallback_reason (enum: capacity, error, cost_policy, region_unavailable, preempt), selected_variant (string), total_path_ms (int), sampled_trace_id (string), tenant_id (string), redaction_flag (bool). Keep fields flat and short to minimize storage.

Storage/ingest considerations: use the existing telemetry kinesis stream with a new compressed topic for breadcrumbs. Explore protobuf vs compact CSV string; start with compact CSV-in-JSON for rapid rollout. Provide configuration to disable breadcrumbs per-tenant. Privacy: never include prompt text by default.

Rollout plan: 1) Feature branch + unit tests (routing service) 2) Staging deploy with 1% deterministic sampling for selected tenants 3) Console UX behind feature flag and enable to internal prod tenants 4) Ramp sampling and default retention settings 5) Document in runbook and update escalation guides.

2026-03-07 - Priya Sengupta (console): UX mockups attached to design doc; recommends adding a condensed latency waterfall and highlighting the hop that triggered fallback.
